summary: Residual version-lock remains after shadow-mirroring abort, causing implicit legacy routing
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightRoute AI reported that after an attempted canary + shadow-mirroring rollout (promote -> shadow traffic -> abort), a subset of tenant requests continued to be routed to the legacy pinned version despite the canary being rolled back.

Impact:
- ~8% of requests from BrightRoute's production tenant were served by the legacy variant for ~30 minutes after the abort.
- Observed mixed outputs and intermittent tokenization deltas leading to downstream application errors and a brief billing discrepancy.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool for BrightRoute in us-west-2.
- Orchestrator version: v1.12.7.
- Edge-proxy: v3.4.2.
- Serving runtime: release-2025-11.

Steps to reproduce (customer report + internal repro):
1) Customer requested a canary rollout of redwood-v2-compat-7B with shadow-mirroring enabled for 10% traffic.
2) Prewarm and shadow started successfully; traffic mirrored to community-llama-70b-q4 for profiling.
3) At 10:23 UTC, customer aborted the rollout due to quality regression. Abort sequence initiated via console (rollout abort).
4) Control-plane reported abort complete at 10:24 UTC, but edge-mesh continued to serve legacy variant for ~30 minutes for a cohort of session tokens.
5) Repro by replaying session tokens from request logs shows consistent legacy variant routing for those tokens until a manual cache flush at 10:55 UTC.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Orchestrator logs show a successful abort and snapshot commit: "snapshot_commit: rollback -> epoch 8421".
- Edge-proxy logs show repeated 200 responses but with header X-Model-Version: redwood-v1-locked (legacy) for token cohort.
- Routing-mesh trace for a sampled request: "route-lookup -> route-cache hit -> affinity-token resolved to cohort-A -> model-binding: legacy" despite control-plane snapshot pointing to non-legacy binding.
- KV cache metrics show mismatched TTLs between edge cache and orchestrator snapshot: edge TTL remained at 12h, orchestrator snapshot epoch had a TTL of 30s for ephemeral binds.

Initial hypothesis:
- Shadow-mirror abort triggered a fast commit on the control plane, but the edge routing-mesh retained a stale affinity cache entry for a cohort of session tokens because prewarm shadowing wrote a long-lived binding in the edge cache. The longer TTL prevented expected unpin/unbind flows, causing implicit legacy routing.
- Possible race between cache-invalidation messages and the orchestrator's epoch bump, where the edge accepted the shadow prewarm write (with an undocumented TTL override) and ignored the subsequent rollback invalidate due to backpressure on the invalidation queue.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Support triggered a targeted cache invalidation for BrightRoute tenant cohort via edge admin API at 10:55 UTC which restored expected routing.
- We notified customer and opened this ticket for root-cause and broader mitigation.

Next steps:
- Engineering to verify invalidation queue metrics and whether backpressure led to dropped invalidation messages.
- Add telemetry to detect cohort-level routing divergence within 5 minutes of rollout abort.
- Short-term: tighten prewarm shadow write TTLs to 1 minute for dedicated-rollouts to avoid long-lived bindings.
- Postmortem to propose control-plane -> edge invalidation acknowledgements for committed rollbacks.

Notes:
- Customer reported a small billing spike due to additional served tokens while legacy variant was active; finance notified for adjustment pending final RCA.
- See linked GH PRs for an in-progress change to edge invalidation handling.
comments: 2025-11-18 - Sofia Chen (Support): Initial customer report received via support email at 10:30 UTC. Logged request ids and sample session tokens. Marked as P1 due to production quality regression.
2025-11-18 - Maya Kapoor (SRE): Confirmed abort was recorded in control-plane at 10:24 UTC. Collected edge-proxy and orchestrator traces. Observed TTL mismatch in edge write path.

2025-11-18 - Kenji Tanaka (Serving Runtime): Found evidence that prewarm flow includes an optional TTL override when shadow-mirroring is enabled. We didn't anticipate this being set on dedicated prewarm; raising PR to cap TTL for shadow writes.
2025-11-19 - Maya Kapoor (SRE): Triggered targeted cohort invalidation; customer confirms routing corrected at 10:58 UTC. Monitoring for reoccurrence; no recurrence so far.
2025-11-19 - Product (Ava Martinez): Request to add a rollout post-check to verify no cohort-level bindings remain after abort; will coordinate with engineering for telemetry dimension specs.

2025-11-20 - Engineering (PR note): gh:inference/orchestrator#4321 opened to ensure rollback sends explicit invalidation messages and retries on queue backpressure. Edge change gh:edge/proxy#508 will cap prewarm TTL and surface backpressure metrics.
2025-11-20 - Support (Sofia Chen): Customer update drafted; offering credit for extra tokens pending RCA. Asked finance to hold invoice adjustment until engineering confirms fix timeline.
resolution: Mitigation: targeted cache invalidation done; short-term fix to cap prewarm TTL deployed to staging. Long-term fix (invalidation ACKs + retries) in PR review. Pending full RCA and postmortem.
follow_up_actions: Deploy edge TTL cap to prod for dedicated prewarm flows
Add invalidation ack telemetry and alerting
Conduct postmortem and update rollout runbook
Finance: reconcile billing delta with BrightRoute
